title: Words in Context, Part 1: The Method and Two Questions

beats.say: Words in context questions give you a sentence with a blank, and ask for the most logical and precise word or phrase to fill it.

card.text: The most logical and precise word

beats.say: The words range from everyday words, such as reserved, to harder words, such as ephemeral. But the method is the same for all of them.
The key idea is that the text always contains a clue. Your job is to find the clue that tells you what the blank must mean.
Step one. Cover the choices, and read the whole text, including the part that comes after the blank.
beats.item: Cover the choices; read it all

beats.say: Step two. Find the clue. It may be a contrast, a restatement, or a cause and effect.
Step three. Put your own word in the blank first, even a rough word like quiet, or not lasting.
Step four. Eliminate choices of the wrong direction, positive or negative. Then pick the one that matches your word most precisely.

scenes.title: Clue words and what they mean

beats.say: A colon, a dash, or the phrase that is, introduces an explanation. The blank should match the explanation that follows.
Words like unlike, although, and but signal a contrast. The blank should mean the opposite of the contrasted idea.
Words like because, so, and thus signal cause and effect. The blank must be logically connected to the cause or to the effect.
Words like and, also, and similarly signal agreement. The blank should match the tone of the nearby idea.
Easy question. The sentence begins with the word unlike. That is a contrast clue, so the blank will mean the opposite of the crowded market.

scenes.title: Read the sentence
scenes.text: Unlike the crowded downtown market, the farm stand on Route Nine was ______, with only a single table and a handwritten price list.

beats.say: The market is crowded, and the word unlike tells us the farm stand is not. So the blank means not crowded, or small.
The last part confirms it. Only a single table, and a handwritten list. Our word is small and simple.

scenes.title: Which word fits the blank?
scenes.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?

beats.say: Choice A, bustling, means busy. That is the opposite of what we need, because the stand is not like the crowded market.
Choice C, expensive, has no support. The text never talks about prices being high.
Choice D, famous, has no support either. Nothing in the sentence is about fame.
Choice B, modest, means small and simple. It matches our word and the clue. The answer is B.
Medium question. Here the clue is a restatement. After the blank, the text explains the word in other words. We use the explanation as our prediction.

scenes.title: Read the sentence
scenes.text: The lake in the valley was ______ in the summer, appearing only after heavy rain and drying up within a few days.

beats.say: The sentence explains how the lake behaves. It appears only after heavy rain, and it dries up within a few days.
beats.underline: drying up within a few days

beats.say: So the blank means not lasting, or short-lived. That is our own word before we look at the choices.

scenes.title: Which word fits the blank?
scenes.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?

beats.say: Choice A, permanent, means lasting forever. The lake dries up in days, so this is the opposite.
Choice C, enormous, is about size. The text gives no size, only how long the lake lasts.
Choice D, polluted, is about dirt. The text does not mention the water quality.
Choice B, temporary, means not lasting. It matches our prediction exactly. The answer is B.
To recap. Cover the choices, find the clue, and put your own word in the blank first.
Contrast words flip the meaning, and a restatement defines the blank. Cross out the wrong direction first.
